summary: Nine experiments completed in 3.1 minutes, including five compute-bound experiments. Rebudgeted adapter-withheld ARC LOO cell was the longest listed compute-bound experiment at 2.2 minutes, but no data available this milestone explains its phase-level cause or establishes a parallel multi-model dispatch opportunity.
bottlenecks_identified: Rebudgeted adapter-withheld ARC LOO cell set the critical path at 2.2 minutes, but no data available this milestone identifies why it took longest.
Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks the listed experiments but supplies no phase-level timing for setup, model loading, inference, or teardown.
The GPU report is not correlated to individual experiment windows, so it cannot establish utilization efficiency during the compute-bound tasks.
No data available this milestone establishes that a compute-bound task loaded two or more models in parallel or missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic start, stop, and phase spans from every experiment instead of relying on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Capture per-GPU utilization samples with the active experiment identity and phase attached.
Write a launch receipt that records model count, intended concurrency, selected GPU, and runner choice; select DualGPURunner only when two or more models are loaded in parallel.
Profile the 2.2-minute Rebudgeted adapter-withheld ARC LOO cell before choosing a runtime optimization.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add experiment-scoped monotonic phase timing to localize the 2.2-minute critical path.
Add task-correlated GPU telemetry so compute-window utilization can be distinguished from an end-state snapshot.
Add model-count and runner-choice launch receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for two-or-more-model parallel work only.
meta_reflection: The timing evidence identifies the duration leader but does not explain its cost. The locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator is false, and no data available this milestone shows a two-or-more-model parallel task or a DualGPURunner miss, so instrumentation should precede optimization claims.
